description: Circular regulatory sign with a wide red border on a white face, posting a speed limit in kilometres per hour.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Slim galvanised post carrying a flat circular plate near the top, plate face white with a wide solid red annular border band around its full circumference and a large bold black numeral 90 filling the white centre, plate mounted square across the post Materials: White retroreflective sheeting yellowed and chalky with age, red border paint faded toward orange on the sun-facing side, galvanised post with rust at the ground line, road spatter on the lower plate.

Legend: this object is a SIGN, and its printed legend is part of the object, not an annotation on the photograph. Render every letter, numeral, pictogram, arrow and coloured band described above, exactly as described and nothing more. Thai script must be rendered as Thai script with correct glyph shapes, above the roman line where both are described. Lettering and pictograms lie flat on the sign face, sharp, high-contrast and correctly proportioned, and the face must stay legible despite the camera angle. Do not leave the face blank, do not substitute lorem or invented wording, and do not add any text that was not described.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no drop shadow, and no border around the photograph itself.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Two-component sign built to the declared 0.600 x 2.300 x 0.080 m, measured by the harness, not estimated. 444 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 2, 2 unique geometries of 2, one texture, createObjectModel returning in 37 ms. The passes were worked as ONE build with the deterministic gates run once over the finished prop rather than per pass, so this entry records the same evidence set for each pass: the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not, and that is stated rather than implied. Two corrections were taken and both are recorded. First, the spangle noise was re-keyed from vertex INDEX to quantised POSITION - on a non-indexed buffer an index key gives the three corners of every triangle different values, and the post rendered as a patchwork of flat facets. Second, the rust ramp was re-measured after the first version faded rust in from 1.5 m in a desaturated grey-brown, an artefact of trimming a crop that held both rust and clean coating; splitting the two populations by hue put the rust at #6E5641 confined below 0.30 m with a hard splash line.

featureReviews.evidence: 72 radial segments. The rim reads as a true circle at every azimuth in the 8-frame turntable, and edge-on at 90/270 it reads as a thin plate rather than a wedge. 288 of the prop's 444 triangles are here, which is the only place they were spent.

Graded against the DECLARED registry contract, which is this prop's target, and not against the plate. The harness measured the built bounds at 0.600 x 2.300 x 0.080 m against a declared 0.6 x 2.3 x 0.08 - exact on all three axes, with the flange foot setting the depth exactly as the Meshy proxy's band scan predicted (its lowest band is its deepest, 0.073 of height against the disc bands' 0.008 to 0.041). Disc centre at 1.98 m is a real regulatory mounting height. THE PLATE DISAGREES AND IS NOT BEING MATCHED: the plate and its Meshy proxy both render the disc at 0.44-0.45 of total height (a ~1.0 m disc), which is not a real regulatory proportion for a 0.6 m sign. A reviewer comparing render to plate will see a visibly smaller disc; that is the intended result, is recorded in assumptions and risks, and is the reason this feature is graded against the contract rather than against the image.

Rim band 1.00R-0.95R, red annulus 0.95R-0.717R and cream ground inside it, all taken off the x=515 scanline rather than estimated; numerals at the plate's measured 1.13R width; two bolt heads at 0.74R. All four ride one UV atlas on one material, so the printed front and the bare aluminium back cost one draw call between them - confirmed in the 180 render, which shows a plain grey disc.

CORRECTED during the build. The first ramp faded rust in from 1.5 m at #7D6C5F, both wrong, because the crop trimmed to produce it contained rust AND clean coating. Separating the populations by hue gives rust #6E5641/#72553E confined below 0.30 m, with a per-band orange-pixel count reading 0 percent from 0.44 m to 1.08 m and 56 percent at 0.23 m. Shaft raised to 16 height segments so the splash line lands on a segment boundary and resolves as an edge. Held short of 0.9 because the plate's heavy white spangle STREAKING is not reproduced - the vertex ramp carries the vertical trend and a low-amplitude blotch, not the streaks.

Shaft runs 0.018 m to 2.28 m, past the back of the disc, capped by a 0.02 m bracket to 2.30 m and landing on a 0.16 x 0.018 x 0.08 m flange. Visible in the 180 render. The cap peeks only ~20 mm above the disc's top edge where the plate shows a more prominent bracket.

notes: Budget: maxDrawCalls raised 1 -> 2 in the blockout, not optimised into at the end. The asset already carried maxMaterials=2 and maxUniqueGeometries=2, which are unreachable at one draw call, since one component carries one material. The printed sign disc and the galvanised post+flange assembly are different materials and cannot merge; sibling elephant-crossing-sign ships at d=2/m=3/g=3 for the same reason. Scale: the reference plate and its Meshy proxy both put the disc at 0.44x total height (~1.0 m). The declared 0.6 m disc on a 2.3 m post is the correct real-world regulatory proportion and is what was built, so the plate is proportionally wrong and the model is not.
